content: Peripheral retinal ablation is a treatment used for premature infants diagnosed with threshold retinopathy of prematurity (ROP). This condition, if left untreated, can lead to severe visual impairment or blindness. The objective of this study was to determine whether peripheral retinal ablation, performed using any method, reduces the likelihood of adverse ophthalmic outcomes in these infants. To address this question, a comprehensive search was conducted using the Cochrane Neonatal Review Group's standard methodology. This included searching databases such as the Cochrane Neonatal Group Register of Clinical Trials, MEDLINE, and EMBASE, as well as reviewing previous studies, conference abstracts, expert opinions, and cross-referenced bibliographies. The search terms included Retinopathy of Prematurity, Retrolental Fibroplasia, Lightcoagulation, and Cryosurgery. The selection criteria focused on studies involving premature infants with threshold ROP. These studies had to use random or quasi-random allocation to either a treatment group receiving peripheral retinal ablation of the avascular retina or a control group. Independent assessment of outcomes was required. After a methodological review, only studies employing random allocation were included for data extraction. The validity and relevance of the studies were assessed by two authors, who reached a consensus. Each author independently extracted clinical outcomes from the selected studies. Data analysis followed the standards established by the Cochrane Neonatal Review Group. Two randomized trials were identified and analyzed. The results demonstrated that peripheral retinal ablation significantly reduces the risk of several adverse outcomes. Specifically: 1. The risk of early unfavorable retinal structure decreased from 47.9% in the control group to 28.1% in the treated group, representing an absolute risk reduction of 19.8% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 27.9% to 11.8%). 2. The risk of unfavorable retinal structure in early childhood decreased from 44.3% in the control group to 26.3% in the treated group, with an absolute risk reduction of 18% (95% CI: 27.0% to 9.1%). 3. The risk of unfavorable visual acuity in early childhood decreased from 63% in the control group to 50.6% in the treated group, corresponding to an absolute risk reduction of 12.2% (95% CI: 21.2% to 3.1%). However, it was noted that the visual fields in sighted eyes were slightly smaller in the treated group (mean visual field: 51.3° ± 11.8°) compared to the control group (mean visual field: 58.2° ± 14.5°). In conclusion, peripheral retinal ablation is effective in reducing the incidence of adverse ophthalmic outcomes in premature infants with threshold ROP. However, in sighted eyes, this treatment may result in a slight reduction in the size of the visual field. The long-term outcomes of this intervention remain uncertain at this time.
